global_events: Risk sentiment is cautiously mixed overnight as the US signals additional tariffs targeting India, China, and other nations, while Beijing dismissed the move as politically motivated rather than economically justified. Japan's core inflation climbed to its highest level this year after energy subsidies expired, adding pressure on the Bank of Japan's policy path. Meanwhile, Nvidia's Jensen Huang rejoins the ranks of high-profile executive comebacks, underscoring continued optimism around AI-driven tech demand.
central_banks: All eyes in India are on the upcoming RBI policy verdict, with domestic bond yields edging marginally upward even as crude oil prices stabilised, suggesting markets are pricing in a cautious but potentially accommodative stance. Japan's surging consumer prices complicate the global central bank narrative, keeping rate-path uncertainty elevated across major economies.
policy_sentiment: The Trump administration's renewed tariff threats against India alongside China and others could weigh on export-oriented sectors and currency sentiment, though the rupee has already staged a sharp recovery of 56 paise to 92.29 against the dollar. Separately, the RBI is reportedly investigating a potential multi-million dollar loophole in how importers structure foreign exchange transactions, signalling tighter regulatory scrutiny on FX flows.
